Whoever drives or attempts to drive a motor vehicle while having alcohol exceeding 30 mg per 100 ml of blood detected by a breath analyser, or while under the influence of a drug to such an extent as to be incapable of exercising proper control over the vehicle, is punishable for the first offence with imprisonment for a term up to six months, or with a fine up to two thousand rupees, or with both [1]. For a second or subsequent offence committed within three years of the previous similar offence, the punishment is imprisonment for a term up to two years, or a fine up to three thousand rupees, or with both [1].

- For money payable for money lent, the period of limitation is three years, and the period begins to run when the loan is made, as provided in Article 19 of the Limitation Act, 1963 [2].
- For money lent under an agreement that it shall be payable on demand, the period of limitation is three years, and the period begins to run when the loan is made, as provided in Article 21 of the Limitation Act, 1963 [4].
- When the lender has given a cheque for the money, the period of limitation is three years, and the period begins to run when the cheque is paid, as provided in Article 20 of the Limitation Act, 1963 [6].

rows.answer:
Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine, according to Section 302 of The Indian Penal Code, 45 of 1860 [1]. The same punishment is provided under Section 302 of The Indian Penal Code (Chandigarh), which states that whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine [1].

Related provisions:
- Section 303 of The Indian Penal Code, 45 of 1860, regarding punishment for murder by life-convict, which states that whoever, being under sentence of imprisonment for life, commits murder shall be punished with death [3].
